missionPremise: Smart Files is a BUILD, not a rendering pass (OPS-17 amendment A-002, line 189), and it is a NEW atom family that does not extend brokerage_workspaces (amendment A-012, line 199). Doc 34 approved claims are NOT revised; the build is made true (A-003, line 190). The premise rests on a schema fact re-verified by this lane at source, not inherited: brokerage_workspace_attachments cannot carry store-once-place-many or revise-with-history.
completionPredicate: G-14 is done when a Smart Files contract type and artifact store exist such that (1) one document row supports N placements with the artifact row count invariant under re-placement, (2) a revision supersedes without destroying and the prior version is retrievable by version identity, (3) every served artifact carries source plus computedAt plus servedAt with a STALE indicator proven able to fire by backdate test AND proven silent on a fresh artifact, (4) accessPolicy is a column on the record resolved at read time, and (5) the entityId shape is written down in a decision record before the first schema PR. A stranger evaluates this by running the probes in the frozen WDLL subset, not by reading a PR.
scopeBasis: The dispatch scopes this to G-14 plus lane A half of G-10 and explicitly excludes G-20, G-34, G-44, G-53. The existing ten-item WDLL draft card is scoped to five rows. Carrying it whole would grade this lane on rows the dispatch declared out of scope; authoring a second card would produce two non-comparable cards for one lane (DEV_PROCESS 3.3b). Therefore a SUBSET is frozen, and the boundary is drawn at the artifact-store contract: what the store must structurally guarantee is IN; what is put into it (corpus), what is counted from it (coverage), what is served from it (surface), and what is sold on it (collateral) are OUT.

straddleRulings.ruling: CARRIED with the probe re-pointed from the deployed serving path to the store read path, exercised in-process. The freshness CONTRACT and the proven ability of the STALE indicator to fire are in scope; proving it on a deployed revision is deferred to G-53 item 9. Ruled deliberately rather than silently narrowed, per the dispatch instruction.
straddleRulings.residual: The G-53 lane must re-probe on the serving revision. A store-level pass does NOT satisfy DEV_PROCESS 4.4.

straddleRulings.ruling: CARRIED, and retained deliberately. This is the migration-merged-is-not-applied trap. The applied check stays in this lane card because a store nobody can write to is not a store.

findings.title: The atom contract dependency in legacy-design-tools is a VENDORED TARBALL of the dead package name, 16 minor versions behind npm latest
findings.evidence: artifacts/api-server/package.json:19 reads "@hauska/atom-contract": "file:../../vendor/hauska-atom-contract-1.6.0.tgz". vendor/ holds 1.2.0, 1.4.0, 1.5.0, 1.6.0 tarballs. Neither node_modules/@hauska/atom-contract nor node_modules/@empressaio/atom-contract resolved in this checkout. npm latest for @empressaio/atom-contract is 1.22.0; source repo is at 1.20.0.
findings.why_it_matters: The dispatch asked me to establish what is actually current before building against either. The answer is that legacy-design-tools does not consume the published contract at all on either name - it consumes a local file: tarball pinned at 1.6.0. Building a new family type into @empressaio/atom-contract would NOT reach the lane own repo without also cutting the vendored dependency over. That is a real sequencing dependency the brief did not contain, and it is the DEV_PROCESS 6.3 shape: correct live state resting on something not durable.
findings.disposition: Raised to operator as routing question OR-A1; NOT unilaterally remediated (DEV_PROCESS 5.4). It changes where the contract type is authored and how it is consumed, which is a G-14 sequencing decision.

findings.title: Two pre-existing document tables already exist in legacy-design-tools, and one of them already does content-addressing and access_policy
findings.evidence: lib/db/src/schema/attachedDocuments.ts (attached_documents: id, engagementId notNull FK cascade, title, documentType, extractedText, originalBlobRef documented as 'Reference to the stored original blob (CID / storage key)', actorId, createdAt) and lib/db/src/schema/dataroomDocumentAtoms.ts (dataroom_document_atoms, 107 lines, carries atom_did, entity_type, access_policy, storage_relation, widthed confidence, verification_status, source_document_cid, unique index on (document_id, atom_did) for idempotent upsert; header documents an engine POST /v1/document-ingest pipeline and a deliberate tenant-private clamp firewall).
findings.why_it_matters: The brief premise is that the promise is structurally impossible on brokerage_workspace_attachments. That is TRUE and re-verified. But the brief presents that table as the only relevant prior art, and it is not. There is an existing document ingest path with CID-based content addressing, deterministic DIDs, access-policy clamping, and idempotent re-ingest already built and wired to the engine. Designing the Smart Files store without reading it risks building a fifth parallel document store - precisely the operate-not-rebuild failure the FLEET-L3 ruling names.
findings.important_caveat: attached_documents is NOT a candidate to extend. Read at source, it has the SAME structural defect: a single notNull engagement FK with cascade delete, no updated_at, no version, no access_policy. It is engagement-scoped, not city-scoped, and its own header calls it read-only on the L2 surface. The reusable asset is the CID plus document-ingest MECHANISM and the dataroom atom provenance/policy column shape, NOT the parent table.
findings.disposition: Feeds the design directly. Recorded as a finding because the brief premise section would have led a lane straight past it.

findings.title: ACCESS_POLICY_SCHEMA is defined three times in the contract source - a paired-control divergence risk
findings.evidence: grep -rln 'ACCESS_POLICY_SCHEMA = z.enum' src/ returns src/conformance/common.ts, src/encumbrances/common.ts, src/workspace/common.ts. The canonical type AccessPolicy is declared once at src/registration.ts:56, but the runtime zod enum is re-literalled per subtree. encumbrances additionally narrows to a two-value EncumbranceAccessPolicy at src/encumbrances/common.ts:82.
findings.why_it_matters: DEV_PROCESS 2.4: when one rule has two implementations, the divergence test IS the control. This is one rule with three implementations and no divergence test. A sixth access-policy value, or a reordering, propagates to some subtrees and not others silently. The Smart Files family adding a fourth copy would make it worse.
findings.disposition: The Smart Files type will IMPORT the shared enum rather than re-literal it. The pre-existing triplication is out of this lane scope and is proposed for the durable backlog (DEV_PROCESS 5.3), not fixed here.

findings.title: The workspace family is exported on a subpath, not the root index
findings.evidence: package.json exports map has './workspace' pointing to ./dist/workspace/index.js. grep -n 'workspace' src/index.ts returns zero lines.
findings.why_it_matters: A reader checking whether the contract exports workspace via the root index gets an empty result and could write it up as an absence. DEV_PROCESS 4.3: an empty result is not an absence. Recorded so the next lane does not re-derive it wrongly.

challenges.challenge: Does A-012 actually leave the G-10 lane A half open, or is this dispatch asking for work already ruled?
challenges.resolution: PARTIALLY ALREADY RULED. A-012 (OPS-17:199) rules the EXTEND-vs-SUPERSEDE question: NEW family, does not extend brokerage_workspaces. But OPS-17:131 states the G-10/S-6 instrument as 'Written ruling plus contract types; no shape reconstructed from parts anywhere in lane code', and S-6 (OPS-17:92) requires DECLARING entityId shapes for non-parcel node classes. A-012 does not state an entityId shape. So the remaining lane A half of G-10 is the entityId shape declaration only. Recorded so the close is not graded against a ruling that was already made before dispatch.

challenges.challenge: The brief says the store must make three doc-34 sentences true. Is the store alone sufficient for that?
challenges.resolution: NO, and the card reflects it. A store that structurally supports store-once-place-many does not make 'a document lives once and appears everywhere it belongs' TRUE for a customer until a corpus is in it and a surface serves it. Those are G-44 and G-53. This lane completionPredicate is deliberately the structural guarantee, not the customer-visible claim. Stated explicitly so the close is not read as satisfying A-003.

challenges.challenge: Is no-UI-in-scope compatible with the item 5 freshness probe?
challenges.resolution: Only after re-pointing the probe to the store read path. Ruled under straddleRulings; the residual obligation on G-53 is recorded rather than dropped.

challenges.challenge: Could the STALE indicator be built so it cannot fail for the right reason?
challenges.resolution: This is the DEV_PROCESS 2.2 trap and the reason the card requires BOTH directions: backdate drives it to fire, AND a fresh artifact leaves it silent, each asserted on the real exit code and not a pipe exit code (2.3). A one-directional test would pass a permanently-firing indicator.

openToOperator.question: Where is the Smart Files contract type AUTHORED, and how does legacy-design-tools consume it?
openToOperator.basis: A-CP1-F1. legacy-design-tools consumes @hauska/atom-contract via a file: tarball pinned at 1.6.0 while npm latest is @empressaio/atom-contract 1.22.0. There is no path by which a type added to the published contract reaches this lane repo without a dependency change.
options: Author in @empressaio/atom-contract and cut legacy-design-tools over from the vendored 1.6.0 tarball to the published package (larger blast radius, fixes the drift, touches 54-dependent territory adjacent to the backlogged rename)
Author in @empressaio/atom-contract and vendor a new tarball under the new name (keeps the vendoring pattern, does not fix the drift, is DEV_PROCESS 6.3 debt by construction)

Author the Smart Files type locally in legacy-design-tools first and promote it to the contract after the shape settles (fastest to a working store; risks a second source of truth, which is DEV_PROCESS 6.2)
openToOperator.plannerRecommendation: Option 3 for the first iteration of the type, with a named promotion step, on the condition that the local type imports the shared accessPolicy enum rather than re-declaring it. Rationale: the shape is genuinely unsettled, and freezing an unsettled shape into a published cross-repo contract is the more expensive mistake. But this is a sequencing decision with cross-repo consequences and it is the operator call, not mine.
openToOperator.blocking: Blocks the first schema PR. Design work proceeds regardless of which option is chosen.

openToOperator.question: Does the Smart Files store reuse the existing document-ingest CID mechanism, or mint its own content addressing?
openToOperator.basis: A-CP1-F2. An engine POST /v1/document-ingest path already produces deterministic CIDs and atom DIDs with access-policy clamping, persisted in dataroom_document_atoms.
openToOperator.plannerRecommendation: Reuse the CID/ingest mechanism, build a new parent table. The parent tables (brokerage_workspace_attachments, attached_documents) both fail on the same single-parent-cascade defect, so neither is extendable; but re-minting content addressing when a deterministic-DID pipeline already exists is the rebuild-instead-of-operate failure.
openToOperator.blocking: Not blocking; shapes the store design. Flagged now because it is cheaper to answer before the schema PR than after.
